links.outcome: Agent detection of tampered patient-identity fields (erroneous inputs) rather than propagating them
links.effect: GPT-4.1 flagged mismatched headers as UNKNOWN in 17.4% of runs but never detected subtle faults; GPT-4.1-nano detected 4.4% of header swaps and <1% of MRN or age changes; GPT-5-chat never identified mismatches.
links.quote: GPT-4.1 flagged mismatched headers as UNKNOWN in 17.4% of runs but never detected subtle faults.

links.outcome: Agents validating inputs before writing into records; copying codes into tampered charts
links.effect: Agents frequently failed, copying codes into tampered charts; subtle tampering (MRN or age changes) passed almost entirely without detection.
links.quote: Agents frequently failed, copying codes into tampered charts.

links.outcome: Agents noticing inconsistent or anomalous inputs and abstaining/notifying
links.effect: Other models rarely abstained; GPT-5-chat never identified mismatches but omitted responses in 12.6% of cases; subtle tampering passed almost entirely without detection.
links.quote: Subtle tampering passed almost entirely without detection.

unlisted_practices: Explicit patient-identity verification in clinical agents before writing to EHR
Benchmarks that treat record integrity (misbinding) as a primary outcome

screen.reason: The study empirically benchmarks the ability of LLM-based clinical agents to detect patient-identity errors (record integrity/tampering) in simulated EHR tool-calling environments.
